correctness.rationale: Reconstructed cover definitions and edge/vertex inequalities; four disjoint cases classify every minimal cover. In nondegenerate case mandatory omitted-rectangle edges and essential selected vertices give binomial weights. In one-sided degenerate case exactly one selected edge per omitted vertex and the corresponding function must be nonconstant; each such cover has size m+n. All vertices is one final cover. Algebra gives the complete polynomial, min coefficient, exact support and top gap. The packaged verifier exhaustively and independently enumerates all labelled vertex-edge subsets for seven cases including 3x4 (2^19 masks), matching every coefficient. Infinite conclusions rely on the proof.

value.rationale: The precise object is the complete inclusionwise-minimal strong-total-cover distribution on complete bicliques, equivalently the minimal domination spectrum of their incidence subdivisions. It extends an important new covering invariant from a known minimum bound and partial structural trichotomy to a full two-parameter coefficient formula and degenerate-case classification. Most notably, it proves arbitrarily long terminal gaps among sizes of inclusionwise minimal dominating sets in a natural family, with a unique largest set; this structural spectrum phenomenon, unlike the known cardinality minimum, has intrinsic graph-theoretic interest.
